decisive_items: PVB19 DNA was found (viral load of 0.2 PVB19 DNA copies/β-globin gene copy, or 33,438 copies/μg of isolated DNA) in lesional skin biopsy specimen, but not in the serum
Serum parvovirus B19 (PVB19) IgM and IgG antibodies were detectable
Standard phototesting with UV-A and UV-B was unremarkable
response.rationale: The lesion-local PVB19 DNA plus serologic IgM/IgG positivity directly implicate parvovirus B19 as the cause, outweighing the sun-exposure timing because phototesting was normal. Erythema multiforme is a plausible clinical mimic but lacks PVB19-specific tissue evidence and its classic target lesions are not described.

rejected.why: Gianotti-Crosti typically shows monomorphic papules, not small blisters/vermillion-border vesicles; PVB19 association is nonspecific and distribution is atypical.
Phototoxic reaction contradicted by unremarkable UV-A/UV-B phototesting and absence of photosensitizer use.
Erythema multiforme is usually less pruritic and often targetoid; PVB19 tissue DNA and serology more directly support viral infection.
